title: Top Things to Do in Kornati, Croatia 2027
metaDescription: Kornati National Park guide for 2027: the Crown cliffs, island cruises, snorkeling, Tureta fortress, ticket prices in euros and tips for planning a visit.
content:
## What Is Kornati National Park?

Kornati National Park is an archipelago in the Adriatic in northern Dalmatia. It covers 89 islands, islets and reefs. Most of the land is bare limestone with dry-stone walls and very little tree cover. There are no bridges and no scheduled ferries, so every visit is by boat. The park is open all year with no gates or fixed hours.

The best months are May, June, July and September. July and August are the busiest, and a sunny day in August can draw many excursion boats to the same few stops.

## Top Attractions in Kornati

### 1. The Crown Cliffs (Kornati Krune)

The Crown cliffs are the main reason people come. These are the outer sea-facing cliffs of islands such as Klobučar and Mana, and they drop almost vertically into deep water. Heights reach roughly 80 m. The best view is from the water, which is why a boat trip or a slow pass by skiff counts as the headline activity. Light is best in the morning and late afternoon, when the rock turns orange and the sea looks darker.

### 2. Kornat Island

Kornat is the largest island in the group, about 25 km long. It is the one island with enough to see on land, including old stone shepherd huts, olive groves and small seasonal settlements. Most of the other islands are uninhabited except for summer visitors.

### 3. Tureta Fortress

Tureta is a ruined Byzantine fortress on Kornat, dating to the 6th century. The walk from the shore is short and uphill. The reward is a wide view of the surrounding islands. Wear closed shoes, since the ground is loose limestone and there is no shade.

### 4. Swimming and Snorkeling

The water around Kornati is very clear, and visibility often exceeds 10 m in summer. Rocky shelves near the shore are good for snorkeling, with sea urchins, small fish schools and seagrass beds. Most day tours include two or three swim stops. If snorkeling is the priority, bring your own mask, since rental gear on boats varies in quality.

### 5. Konoba Lunch on the Islands

A few seasonal konobas, such as those on the sheltered bays of Kornat, serve grilled fish, lamb, local olive oil and sheep cheese. Many are run by families who farm the islands' olive groves in summer. Most are open from about May to September and take few or no cards, so carry cash. A full fish lunch for one usually costs €20–35.

## Best Activities in Kornati

### Boat Cruise Tours

A full-day cruise is the simplest way to see the park. Trips last 8–10 hours and depart from Zadar, Biograd na Moru, Vodice, Murter, Šibenik and Pakoštane. Organised tours generally cost €60–79 per person on the official excursion pages, and some cheaper tours start around €35–40 from Murter. The price covers the boat, park ticket and lunch. Many tours combine Kornati with Telašćica Nature Park and its salt lake, Mir.

### Sailing and Mooring

Kornati is a major sailing area. Buoys are free with a valid ticket, which makes the park easy to explore with a rental boat. Fees are charged by boat length and season. Take care in the shallow channels, where unmarked rocks are common.

### Fishing

Fishing needs a separate licence of €20 for one day or €40 for three days, in addition to the daily boat ticket. Fishing is restricted in the strictly protected zones.

### Hiking

Hiking is limited, since paths are few and shade is almost absent. The Tureta trail on Kornat is the best-known walk. Take at least 1.5 litres of water per person.

## Kornati Ticket Prices (2026–2027)

Park admission is charged per boat, per day, not per person. Organised tours include the ticket in the price.

| Boat length | Low season (Jan–May, Oct–Dec) | High season (Jun–Sep) |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 6.99 m | €25 | €45 |
| 7–10.99 m | €55 | €110 |
| 11–17.99 m | €100 | €200 |
| 18–24.99 m | €240 | €480 |

Buying a ticket from the ranger boat inside the park costs about double the advance price for the smallest class, at €45 or €90. Buy ahead from the park's online shop or at the Murter reception.

Fees for a 35–50 m yacht are €640 for one day in summer, so group charters over 25 m often run into hundreds of euros in park fees alone.

## Is a Tour or Your Own Boat Better?

For most visitors, a tour is the better choice. The ticket, skipper and lunch are covered, and there is no navigation risk. Renting a small boat makes sense for groups of four to six who want a quiet cove and an early start. The private speedboat tours that cost €150 or more per person are usually not worth the extra cost, since the standard tours reach the same cliffs and swim stops.

## Practical Tips

- **Start early.** Boats leave around 8:00–9:00. Early departures mean calmer water and fewer boats at the first stop.
- **Bring shade.** Most of the islands have almost no trees. Pack a hat, sun cream and a light cover-up.
- **Carry cash.** Island konobas often take cash only.
- **Check the wind.** The bora and strong sirocco winds can cancel trips or make the open-sea side rough. Check forecasts the evening before.
- **Respect the rules.** Do not remove stones or shells, light fires or anchor over seagrass. Use buoys where they are provided.
- **Plan one full day.** A day is enough for the headline sights. A sailing trip can last several days at an extra €130 for a 5-day ticket on a boat up to 7 m in summer.

## Frequently Asked Questions

See the FAQ section below for quick answers on tickets, timing and getting there.

faq.question: How much does it cost to visit Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: Organised day tours usually cost about €60–79 per person and include the park ticket and lunch. On your own boat under 7 m, the ticket is €25 in low season and €45 in high season, charged per boat per day.

faq.question: How do you get to Kornati without a boat?
faq.answer: There is no bridge or public ferry, so a boat is required. Excursion boats depart from Zadar, Biograd na Moru, Vodice, Murter, Šibenik and Pakoštane, and most trips last 8–10 hours.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Kornati?
faq.answer: May, June, July and September offer the best mix of warm sea and manageable crowds. July and August are the busiest months, so book tours and park tickets ahead.

faq.question: What are the Kornati Crowns?
faq.answer: The Crowns are steep outer cliffs on the sea-facing edge of islands such as Klobučar and Mana. They rise to roughly 80 m above the water and are best seen from a boat.

faq.question: Can you swim and snorkel in Kornati?
faq.answer: Yes. The water is very clear and most day tours include two or three swim stops. Rocky shores near the islands suit snorkeling, so bring your own mask for a better fit.

faq.question: Do you need a ticket for Kornati if you join a tour?
faq.answer: Every visitor needs a valid ticket for each day in the park. Most organised tours include it in the price, so ask the operator before booking.

faq.question: Is fishing allowed in Kornati National Park?
faq.answer: Fishing is allowed with a licence that costs €20 for one day or €40 for three days. It is charged on top of the daily boat ticket, and restricted zones apply.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Kornati are a boat cruise past the Crown cliffs, swimming and snorkeling in clear bays, climbing to the Tureta fortress on Kornat, and lunch at a seasonal konoba. Day tours cost about €60–79 from Zadar, Biograd, Vodice or Murter, and the park ticket is charged per boat.
